audit.whatIsWrong: Every difficulty line in both layers rests on 'wait until Relentless Pursuit is down'. In this matchup it is almost never down, and nothing said why.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Lucian quickly dashes a short distance. Lightslinger attacks reduce Relentless Pursuit's cooldown.' The base number is 16/15.5/15/14.5/14, but every Lightslinger double-shot shaves it. Waiting is not the plan — denying him autos is what makes the wait finish.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, whys[2], spikes[1].text and wants.you[0] now state the shrink and point the player at denying shots instead of counting to sixteen.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content whys for Level 3 and Level 6 both read as Ambessa windows while the level chart hands both stages to Lucian, and neither carried a real number.
audit.why: The chart gives Lucian five of seven stages, which matches the 47.82% win rate, so the whys were the side that was wrong. At 6 the honest picture is a 130-second Public Execution against a 110-second The Culling: you get one attempt and he gets the lane if you miss. At Levels 4-5 the waits are Lacerate 13s and Repudiation 18s against Piercing Light's 9s.
audit.corrected: whys[2] and whys[4] now agree with the chart, and whys[3] carries the three real cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Public Execution is repeatedly described as blinking 'behind' the target and as carrying 'armor pen and on-ability healing' that pays for the burst.
audit.why: Riot's text: she 'blinks to the farthest enemy champion in a line of her choosing and suppresses them upon her arrival. She then slams the enemy into the ground where they take damage and are stunned.' There is no armour penetration and no healing in that description. The kit file's derived 'heal' flag on her R contradicts Riot's own text, so I dropped the claim rather than build a trade plan on it.
audit.corrected: spikes[2].text, mid, wants.you[0] and whys[4] now describe the blink, the range and the suppression only.

audit.whatIsWrong: Ardent Blaze is never mentioned anywhere in either layer, yet it is what makes Lucian uncatchable after the first item.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Lucian shoots a missile that explodes in a star shape, marking and briefly revealing enemies. Lucian gains Move Speed for attacking marked enemies.' The mark is the kiting engine — the reason the late-game text's 'he usually can keep the fight at distance' is true. It is 900 range on 14/13/12/11/10.
audit.corrected: Added to wants.foe[0], late and whys[6], and the 14s appears in breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[1].why says 'Dash-resets stack your passive shield mid-trade'. Ambessa's passive does not shield.
audit.why: Drakehound's Step grants her next attack bonus range, damage and attack speed and refunds energy — no shield. The shield is Repudiation, and its real property is the one that matters here: damage she blocks while bracing increases the slam. Lucian's Lightslinger double-shot is exactly the dense non-minion damage that pays for it.
audit.corrected: Rewrote phases[1].why and whys[5] around the brace.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Jungle Interaction row treats this as a normal lane where you ping for a gank. It never says what a gank on YOU costs.
audit.why: Riot's text on Lightslinger: 'When Lucian is healed or shielded by an ally, or when a nearby enemy Champion is immobilized, his next 2 basic attacks will deal bonus magic damage.' Any hard CC his jungler lands on you turns his next two shots into a burst window on top of the gank. It also means an enemy support or jungler shielding him does the same.

_missing-interactions.json lists a 'needs-antiheal — Lucian sustains through chip damage (Lightslinger (P))' row for this matchup. Riot's Lightslinger text does not heal Lucian; it reacts to being healed or shielded by an ally. In a solo top lane there is nobody to do that, so I did not write anti-heal advice.

edits.before: Lucian owns these levels and you have to respect it. His Lightslinger double-tap plus Piercing Light Q shreds you while you sit on Cunning Sweep alone — no second ability to chain into an empowered auto, and your energy gate means you can't threaten much back. Don't walk up for a Q you can't follow; last-hit at the edge of your cone and eat the chip. The trap is forcing a level-2 trade: he just Relentless Pursuit dashes out of your E slow and keeps shooting. Wait for level 3, and only commit if he burns his dash on the wave or to chase a CS.
edits.after: Lucian owns these levels and you have to respect it. His Lightslinger double-tap plus Piercing Light Q shreds you while you sit on Cunning Sweep alone — no second ability to chain into an empowered auto, and your energy gate means you can't threaten much back. Don't walk up for a Q you can't follow; last-hit at the edge of your cone and eat the chip. The trap is forcing a level-2 trade: he just Relentless Pursuit dashes out of your E slow and keeps shooting. Wait for level 3 — his dash is 16s at rank 1, but every Lightslinger shot shaves it, so denying autos is what makes it stay down.

edits.before: Level 6 is your moment and basically your only clean kill window in lane. Public Execution blinks you behind the farthest enemy in the line and suppresses him through his Relentless Pursuit dash — the dash he normally uses to escape your gap-close can't save him once you're already past him. Bait the dash first (CS pressure or a fake Q step-up), then R, suppress, slam, and chain Q-Sundering-Slam plus E-spin with R's armor-pen passive healing you through it. Levels 4-5 before that are your worst window — longest cooldowns, his poke unanswered — so farm and hold R for the all-in.
edits.after: Level 6 is your moment and basically your only clean kill window in lane. Public Execution blinks 1250 to the farthest champion in the line and suppresses on arrival — a suppressed Lucian cannot dash, cannot shoot and cannot start The Culling. Bait the dash first (CS pressure or a fake Q step-up), then R, suppress, slam, and chain Q-Sundering-Slam plus E-spin while he is still locked. Levels 4-5 before that are your worst window — Lacerate 13s, Repudiation 18s, his poke unanswered — so farm and hold R for the one all-in you get.

edits.before: This drifts back to him as the lane settles into items. Once Lucian completes his first crit item and stacks range with Doran's, he out-DPSes your Eclipse all-in if he keeps the fight at distance — and his Lightslinger pace plus Relentless Pursuit means he usually can. Your R is on cooldown most of the time, and a single R kited out leaves you naked with physical-only damage. Your realistic win is to convert that level 6 kill into a lead and end before his item curve overtakes you; if it goes even, look to roam and group rather than re-dueling a fed Lucian who just walks backward and shoots.

notes: The two suspectNames flagged for this matchup ('Hold Relentless Pursuit', 'His Lightslinger') are both false positives — those are Lucian's real ability names. The real errors were elsewhere: Ambessa's R was credited with armour penetration and healing that Riot's description does not give it, and Drakehound's Step was credited with a shield that belongs to Repudiation. Her kit file's derived 'heal', 'grounding' and 'zone' flags on Public Execution all contradict its own description, so I made none of those claims. I also did not write the _missing-interactions 'needs-antiheal' row: Lightslinger reacts to an ally healing or shielding Lucian, which does not happen in a solo lane.
